newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SAFRICA GOES INTO MOURNING OVER DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SAFRICA GOES INTO MOURNING OVER DEFEAT.

text.p: South Africa's 25-16 defeat by the British Lions in Cape Town on Saturday was greeted as a national disaster in the weekend's newspapers.

"Boks Blow It" was the front page headline in the Cape Town Sunday Argus while the leading national newspaper -- The Sunday Times -- devoted its front page lead to the defeat next to a colour picture of celebrating Lions fans.
"Boks: What went wrong?" it asked before adding, in a second headline, "Rugby bosses have much to put right after SA's crash at Newlands."
Only the more measured Sunday Independent chose not to make mention of the game on its front page.
More realistically in their back page headlines they said: "It all goes wrong for South Africa and Carel du Plessis as mistakes clutter a woeful first test performance."
However, reports chose to overlook the fact that the defeat was the first for the Springboks in eight matches and that they can still win the series with two tests still to come.

In addition, the fact that the South Africans led for all but nine minutes of the game before Lions scrum-half Matt Dawson scored a 72nd minute lead to put his side into a match-winning lead was also ignored in the obituaries.
"South African rugby is today headed for another crisis," said the Sunday Argus's front page story.

"The match served as Carel du Plessis's introduction to coaching at the highest level and the tactical naivety and complete non-adherence to the basics of the game are sure to pose question-marks over his future in the position."
This was only du Plessis's second match in charge after a 74-10 victory over Tonga since his appointment in February in succession to Andre Markgraaff.
The Sunday Times saw a wider malaise with South African rugby underestimating the Lions and suffering from provincialism in selection and preparation.
Only in the Sunday Independent did the performance of the Lions merit star billing.

"The British Lions' exhilarating journey of discovery was rewarded in the finest possible way as they doused the Springbok spirit with a performance of quite outstanding control and conviction," they said in their introduction.
The second test is in Durban on Saturday.
